messages:
maya: Quick sync — thinking about our internal API surface for model-serving + Console. Two approaches: (A) gRPC + protobuf between services with generated stubs, or (B) HTTP/JSON everywhere and let the gateway do translation/adapters. Must support per-route quotas, telemetry tags, and header-based rollouts. Pros/cons?

liam: I'm biased towards gRPC internally. Protos give a typed contract and smaller payloads; teams get nice codegen (stubs). Gateway can handle JSON for external clients via transcoding (Envoy).

sara: Proto is great for typing, but generates churn for product SDKs — every proto change = regen + dep bumps. For Console we need flexible quota/policy enforcement and quick UX changes. An adapter at the edge centralizes auth/quotas/metrics so product teams don't need to touch infra code for policy tweaks.

oliver: +1 to a hybrid. Internal gRPC for service-to-service, thin gateway adapters for auth/quotas/telemetry and JSON<->proto translation. Keeps strong contracts internally while remaining flexible at the edge. Example Envoy filter we could use: ```yaml
http_filters:
  - name: envoy.filters.http.grpc_json_transcoder
    typed_config:
      '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.grpc_json_transcoder.v3.GrpcJsonTranscoder
      proto_descriptor: "/etc/protos/model_service.pb"
      services: ["model.Service"]
```

maya: Nice. How does this affect rollout UX? Console product folks want easy canary/A-B routing for model variants and gradual rollouts without touching service code. Any constraints with gRPC?

liam: Not really — gRPC supports metadata headers so we can route on `x-model-variant` or `x-canary` header. Gateway route rules can implement weighted routing. Example route snippet: ```yaml
- match:
    headers:
      - name: x-model-variant
        exact_match: canary
  route:
    weighted_clusters:
      - name: model-canary
        weight: 10
      - name: model-stable
        weight: 90
```

sara: Two operational points: 1) Telemetry — adapter must inject trace id, customer_id, route_id so Console/Optimize can correlate cost and quality. 2) Compatibility — enforce proto evolution rules (no renames, only additive fields) and a compat endpoint pattern for older clients. I don't want product teams forced to regenerate stubs mid-release.

oliver: For compatibility we should publish a proto-evolution doc + CI that validates breaking changes (like github.com/org/proto-lint). Also publish generated stubs to our internal package registry so teams can pin versions easily. If a team can't move to gRPC, we keep an HTTP adapter mapped to the same internal proto.

maya: Good. Owner-wise: Sara can own the proto-evolution guide, Liam can spike the Envoy transcoder + canary routing, and I will coordinate SDK owners to automate stub publishing. Small checklist:
- implement JSON<->proto transcoder in staging gateway
- adapter injects telemetry headers (trace, customer_id, route_id)
- define rollout header semantics and weighted routing rules
- proto-evolution CI + published stubs

sara: I'll draft the proto-evolution doc today and include sample compatibility rules.

liam: I'll do a quick proof-of-concept in staging and post the config. Will try the Envoy transcoder + header-based weighted routing this week.

deploy-bot: CI | api-gateway-adapter: build succeeded for commit 9f2d3a :shipit:

maya: Thanks — will sync with Console PMs on rollout UI knobs (weights, headers, percentages).
